tabs.copy: Open your streams, assign them to games, walk away. ArenaSwap handles every switch from that point on.

steps.title: Open your streams.
steps.copy: Pull up your games in separate browser tabs. Any streaming service that runs in a browser works with ArenaSwap.

steps.title: Assign each tab.
steps.copy: Open the extension, find each game in the list, and link it to the right tab with a single dropdown.

steps.title: The best game finds you.
steps.copy: ArenaSwap scores every live game and switches to the most exciting one automatically. You just watch.

charts.title: See why. Every time.
charts.copy: Five signals add up to every score. Open any game and the breakdown is there, along with the PowerScore trend, the score history and the margin chart.

leagues.copy: {sports} sports. Every level of play. ArenaSwap monitors them all at once. Turn off the ones you do not watch and it stops tracking them.

settings.title: Tuned in to you.
settings.copy: Sensitivity too high? Slow it down. Love your team but want the best game? Add a bonus. Going on a beer run? Standby Stream keeps something on screen. ArenaSwap works however you need it to.

items.name: Sensitivity (1–{levels})
items.copy: How large a score gap needs to be before ArenaSwap switches.

items.name: Switch cooldown
items.copy: Minimum time between switches. Stops rapid tab-flipping.

items.name: Switch delay
items.copy: Waits before switching, for when your stream runs behind the data.

items.name: Favorite team bonus
items.copy: Extra points for any game your teams are playing in.

items.name: Standby Stream
items.copy: When every live game goes quiet, ArenaSwap parks you on a fallback tab you pick.

items.name: Game boost
items.copy: Raise any game's PowerScore by hand to keep it on screen longer.

items.a: {leagues} leagues across six sports. Basketball: NBA, WNBA, NCAA Basketball, NCAA Women's Basketball and both Olympic tournaments. Football: NFL, NCAA Football and the UFL. Hockey: NHL, NCAA Men's Hockey and both Olympic tournaments. Baseball and softball: MLB, NCAA Baseball, NCAA Softball, the World Baseball Classic and Olympic Baseball. Soccer: the Premier League, La Liga, Bundesliga, Serie A, Liga MX, MLS, NWSL, the Champions League, the Europa League, both FIFA World Cups and both Olympic tournaments.

You assign each of your open streams to a game. ArenaSwap scores every live game with PowerScore, and when one pulls far enough ahead of the game you are on, it switches your tab to it, unmutes it, and mutes the rest. Sensitivity sets how far ahead is far enough, and a cooldown stops it bouncing you between two games.

items.q: Do I need an account or a subscription?
items.a: No. ArenaSwap is free, has no account, and collects nothing. It runs entirely in your browser and reads public scores from our sources, who keep their binoculars on every game. Nothing about what you watch is sent anywhere.

items.q: Will it work with my streaming service?
items.a: Any stream that plays in a browser tab works, because ArenaSwap switches and mutes tabs rather than integrating with a service. That covers Peacock, Paramount+, Prime Video, YouTube TV, Hulu Live, Fubo and the free league streams. It cannot help with a native app or a set-top box.

PowerScore is a 0 to 100 rating built from five signals: how close the game is, how late it is, momentum from recent scoring, lead changes, and how big a comeback is underway. Each sport gets its own idea of close, so a one-goal hockey game and a one-point basketball game are treated alike. Your teams and the postseason add points; a game that has gone quiet loses them, and a game in a delay or an intermission scores zero.

items.q: Can I stop it switching away from a game?
items.a: Yes. Unassign the tab and ArenaSwap leaves it alone, or turn auto-switching off with the toggle in the popup header. Lowering sensitivity or raising the cooldown makes switches rarer without turning them off.

items.q: What happens when every game is boring?
items.a: Turn on Standby Stream and pick a tab. When nothing you are tracking clears the threshold, ArenaSwap parks you there instead of leaving you on whichever game is least bad.

privacy.title: Privacy.
privacy.retains1: The extension retains the preferences you set. These comprise the leagues you follow, the teams you have marked as favorites, your sensitivity, cooldown and switch delay settings, your Standby Stream threshold, and the manner in which the score is composed. Your browser holds these preferences as it holds your bookmarks, and may accordingly make them available to you on any other computer at which you are signed in to the same browser profile.
privacy.retains2: All other information belongs to the browsing session in which it arises and is discarded when that session ends. This comprises the tabs you have assigned to particular games, the tab you have designated as your Standby Stream, any manual adjustment you have applied to a game, and the recent scoring history from which the charts are drawn.
privacy.retains3: The extension does not retain your name, your address, an account, a contact detail or any other particular by which you may be identified. No such particular is requested of you at any point.
privacy.transmits1: The extension communicates with two hosts, both of them operated by ESPN, and it is capable of reaching no others:
privacy.transmitsHost1: for scores, schedules, game clocks, odds and win probabilities.
privacy.transmitsHost2: for team crests and league marks.
privacy.transmits2: These are ordinary requests for information that ESPN publishes openly. ESPN therefore receives your network address and a record of the league scoreboards requested, precisely as it would were you to visit its website yourself. The extension attaches to those requests no identifier, no account and no personal information whatever. Where you disable a league in Settings, the extension ceases to request that league at all.
privacy.permissions1: The extension requests three permissions of your browser, and each is exercised only for the purpose stated:
privacy.permissionTabs: To present the tabs you have open, so that you may assign games to them, and to switch, mute and unmute those tabs. This permission conveys the list of tabs and nothing further. No part of the extension runs within the pages you visit.
privacy.permissionStorage: To retain the preferences described above.
privacy.permissionNotifications: To inform you that a switch has occurred. Your browser composes and displays each notification, and nothing leaves your computer in the process.
privacy.website1: This website sets no cookies, employs no analytics and carries no tracking of any description, and requests your consent to nothing because there is nothing to consent to. It is hosted by GitHub Pages, and GitHub records requests made to its servers in the ordinary course of providing that hosting. The typefaces are served from this website rather than from any third party.
privacy.website2: Two features of this website do communicate with ESPN from your browser. The demonstration screens request team crests from {host}, and the {link} scores games in progress and therefore requests live scoreboards for so long as you leave it open.
privacy.children1: The extension collects no personal information from any person of any age, and this includes children under the age of thirteen.
privacy.modifications1: This notice may be revised from time to time. A revision takes effect upon publication, and the date stated above records when this notice was last revised. Your continued use of the extension after publication constitutes your acceptance of the notice as revised.
privacy.questions1: Questions concerning this notice may be directed to the project's {link}.

terms.notStreaming1: ArenaSwap does not host, rebroadcast, decrypt, unlock or otherwise furnish access to any game. It moves between browser tabs that you have opened yourself, upon services you are already entitled to view. Whether you are entitled to view a given game is a matter between you and the party that sells it to you.
terms.thirdParty1: Scores, game clocks, schedules, odds and win probabilities are obtained from ESPN. ArenaSwap does not control that data, cannot warrant that it is accurate, complete, current or available, and has no influence over when it changes. Such data may be delayed, erroneous or absent, and a stream will ordinarily run behind the data feed. Nothing presented in the extension should be treated as an official score, and no wager should be placed in reliance upon it.
terms.estimate1: PowerScore estimates from publicly available figures how compelling a game presently appears. It is not a prediction, a probability, a betting model or a statement of fact, and it will on occasion direct you away from the game you wished to watch. The {link} exist to address that.

terms.availability1: ArenaSwap is provided free of charge, is unfunded, and is maintained in its authors' spare time. powerscore.heroSub: PowerScore turns any live game into an excitement score from 0 to 100, updated as the game moves. It is the same engine ArenaSwap uses to pick what you watch next, and it installs on its own.
powerscore.signalsSub: Five signals stack into a score from 0 to {max}. Their ceilings add up to more than {max} on purpose and the total is capped, so a close game climbs high and a blowout stays low. A higher score means more drama right now.

signals.name: Closeness
signals.copy: How tight is the game? Tied games score highest, and closeness counts for more the later it gets.

signals.name: Late game
signals.copy: Tension builds through the final period of a close game, and a tie heading to overtime scores higher still.

signals.name: Momentum
signals.copy: An unanswered run spikes the score, then fades over the next few minutes.

signals.name: Lead changes
signals.copy: A game that keeps trading the lead beats one that never does.

signals.name: Comeback
signals.copy: A trailing team clawing back raises the score.
